title_en: Zhong Yongyu v. Wang Guang and Lin Rongda — dispute over third-party execution objection
ruling_gist_en: The Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Handling of Execution Objections and Reconsideration Cases by People's Courts are provisions concerning how to handle objections raised by parties during the enforcement procedure. Since the enforcement procedure needs to implement the enforceability of effective judgments, the standard for determining whether an execution objection is established should adhere to a higher and more appearance-based standard. This standard is higher than the standard for determining whether the plaintiff can exclude enforcement in an action for execution objection. Thus, Articles 25 to 28 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Handling of Execution Objections and Reconsideration Cases by People's Courts should be understood in the following sense: if the conditions listed in these provisions are met, the execution objection can be established; if the conditions listed in these provisions are not met, the objector's claim in the action for execution objection may not necessarily be dismissed. Whether it is established should be determined by comparing and comprehensively evaluating the specific circumstances of the case, the rights claimed by the objector, the effectiveness of the enforcement applicant's claim realization, and the executed person's rights over the subject matter of enforcement, so as to determine whether the objector's rights can exclude enforcement.
keywords_en: Civil; Action for execution objection; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Fujian Province; Natural person; Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Handling of Execution Objections and Reconsideration Cases by People's Courts; Whether the agreement on real estate in a divorce agreement can exclude enforcement; Examination standard for actions for execution objection; Partial support; Divorce agreement; Ownership of real estate; Execution objection; Contract dispute; Equity transfer; Lin Rongda third-party execution objection dispute
full_text_en:
钟永玉与王光、林荣达案外人执行异议纠纷案

【Ruling Summary】

The provisions of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Execution Objections and Reconsideration Cases by People's Courts" are rules concerning how to deal with execution objections raised by parties during execution proceedings. Since execution proceedings need to enforce the binding force of effective judgments, a higher and more appearance-based standard of judgment should be adhered to when determining whether an execution objection is established. This standard of judgment is higher than the standard for determining whether a plaintiff can exclude execution in a lawsuit for execution objection. Therefore, the provisions of Articles 25 to 28 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Execution Objections and Reconsideration Cases by People's Courts" should be understood in the following sense: if the conditions listed in these provisions are satisfied, the execution objection can be established; if the conditions listed in these provisions are not satisfied, the request of the objector in the lawsuit for execution objection may not necessarily be untenable. Whether it is established should be determined by comparing and comprehensively judging the specific circumstances of the case, the rights claimed by the objector, the effect of realizing the claim of the applying executor, and the rights of the person subject to execution over the subject matter of execution, so as to determine whether the objector's rights can exclude execution.

Supreme People's Court Civil Judgment

(2015) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 150

Appellant (Original Defendant): Wang Guang, male, Han Chinese, residing in Fuzhou City, Fujian Province.

Agent ad litem: Shi Zheng, lawyer of Fujian Fangyuan Tongyi Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lin Hui, lawyer of Fujian Fangyuan Tongyi Law Firm.

Appellee (Original Plaintiff): Zhong Yongyu, female, She ethnic group, residing in Shanghang County, Fujian Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhuang Zongwei, lawyer of Beijing Dacheng (Xiamen) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Dong Jinhui, lawyer of Beijing Dacheng (Xiamen) Law Firm.

Original Defendant: Lin Rongda, male, Han Chinese, residing in Shanghang County, Fujian Province.

In the case of dispute over execution objection by a third party between appellant Wang Guang and appellee Zhong Yongyu, and original defendant Lin Rongda, Wang Guang, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2014) Min Min Chu Zi No. 7 rendered by the Fujian High People's Court on March 2, 2015, filed an appeal to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a hearing in this case on July 2, 2015. Wang Guang's agent ad litem Shi Zheng and Zhong Yongyu's agents ad litem Zhuang Zongwei and Dong Jinhui appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. Lin Rongda, after being duly summoned, failed to appear. The trial of this case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found through trial: In the case of dispute over equity transfer contract between Wang Guang and Lin Rongda, Wang Guang applied to the court of first instance for property preservation, requesting preservation of Lin Rongda's property pending litigation. On July 15, 2011, the court of first instance rendered the civil ruling (2011) Min Min Chu Zi No. 22-2, freezing Lin Rongda's bank deposits of RMB 57.23 million or sealing up or seizing property of equivalent value, and on July 21, 2011, issued the "Assistance Execution Notice" (2011) Min Min Chu Zi No. 22-2 to the Shanghang County Real Estate Trading Management Office, sealing up a building owned by Lin Rongda located at No. 121 Heping Road, Shanghang County (House Ownership Certificate: Hang Fang Quan Zi No. 06072, hereinafter referred to as the property in dispute), with the sealing period from July 21, 2011 to July 20, 2013.

On December 15, 2011, the court of first instance rendered the civil judgment (2011) Min Min Chu Zi No. 22, ordering Lin Rongda to return the transfer payment of USD 750.681 million (equivalent to RMB 50 million) already paid by Wang Guang. After the civil judgment (2011) Min Min Chu Zi No. 22 became effective, Wang Guang applied to the court of first instance for compulsory execution on December 23, 2012, with the subject matter of execution being USD 750.681 million (equivalent to RMB 50 million) and interest. The court of first instance opened a case for execution on December 24, 2013, and on June 19, 2013, issued the execution ruling (2013) Min Zhi Zi No. 1-4: continuing to seal up the property owned by Lin Rongda located at No. 121 Heping Road, Shanghang County, with the sealing period from July 21, 2013 to July 20, 2014.

On December 5, 2013, Zhong Yongyu, on the grounds that the property in dispute was owned by her, filed an execution objection with the court of first instance, requesting the court to suspend the execution of the property and lift the sealing measures. The court of first instance held that the property in dispute was still registered in the name of Lin Rongda and had not been changed to the name of the third party Zhong Yongyu, so the real right of the said property had not changed and should still belong to Lin Rongda. The third party Zhong Yongyu's claim that the property in dispute was her lawful property lacked factual and legal basis, and the sealing was not improper. The court rendered the execution ruling (2013) Min Zhi Wai Yi Zi No. 3, rejecting Zhong Yongyu's objection. Dissatisfied, Zhong Yongyu filed the present lawsuit.

Zhong Yongyu filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, alleging that the execution ruling (2013) Min Zhi Wai Yi Zi No. 3 made by the court of first instance on December 18, 2013 contained errors in the finding of facts and application of law, and that the execution of the property in dispute should be stopped according to law. The reasons were as follows: On July 22, 1996, Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda signed a "Divorce Agreement", which stipulated that the property in dispute should belong to the woman and her children, but they were only allowed to live in it and not to sell it. After signing the "Divorce Agreement", the two parties went through the divorce registration procedures on August 7 of the same year, but Lin Rongda failed to promptly change the registration of the property in dispute to Zhong Yongyu's name. Despite Zhong Yongyu's repeated requests, no change was made, and the fault lay with Lin Rongda. According to Article 15 of the "Property Law of the People's Republic of China", the "Divorce Agreement" signed by Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda was established according to law, was legally valid, and the property in dispute had always been occupied, controlled, and used by Zhong Yongyu, thus it was Zhong Yongyu's lawful property. According to the provisions of relevant laws and regulations, the property in dispute in this case should not be listed as execution property. The requests were: 1. To confirm that the property in dispute belonged to Zhong Yongyu; 2. To stop the execution of the property in dispute and lift the sealing measures; 3. To bear the litigation costs of this case by Wang Guang and Lin Rongda.

Wang Guang argued in defense: 1. The owner of the property in dispute is Lin Rongda, and the court's execution measures against the property in dispute are correct and lawful. The reasons are as follows: (1) The rights holder on both the "House Ownership Certificate" and the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" for the property in dispute is registered as Lin Rongda, so the real right of the property in dispute belongs to Lin Rongda. (2) Zhong Yongyu claimed that she and Lin Rongda reached a divorce agreement in 1996, which stipulated that "the house with an area of 173 square meters on Heping Road, Chengguan, Shanghang County shall belong to the woman and her minor children, but they are only allowed to live in it and not to sell it." Nearly twenty years have passed since 1996, but the registered owner of the property in dispute is still Lin Rongda, and it still belongs to Lin Rongda. (3) Zhong Yongyu's claim right against Lin Rongda cannot oppose the court's sealing and execution measures, nor can it oppose the applying executor. Zhong Yongyu's request to Lin Rongda to handle the change of registration is factually and legally impossible to realize. Zhong Yongyu's claim to confirm that the property in dispute belongs to her has no factual or legal basis and should be rejected by law. 2. The "Divorce Agreement" cannot serve as the basis for Zhong Yongyu to assert rights. (1) The "Divorce Agreement" stipulates: "The house with an area of 173 square meters on Heping Road, Chengguan, Shanghang County (house number not yet assigned) shall belong to the woman and her minor children. But they are only allowed to live in it and not to sell it." However, according to the "House Ownership Certificate" for the property in dispute, the property has four floors with an area of 748.7 square meters. Therefore, Zhong Yongyu only has a claim right to 173 square meters out of the 748.7 square meters of the property in dispute, and absolutely not to the entire 748.7 square meters. (2) The "Divorce Agreement" specifically states that the 173 square meters are "only allowed to live in, not to sell," indicating that Zhong Yongyu only has the right to live in and use the property, not ownership. (3) The "Divorce Registration Application" submitted by Zhong Yongyu has a blank marriage certificate number, so Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda may not have a valid marriage fact, and the "Divorce Agreement" is invalid. Zhong Yongyu bears the burden of proof for this fact, otherwise she should bear the legal consequences of failing to provide evidence. 3. Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda signed the "Divorce Agreement" as early as 1996, nearly twenty years ago. Zhong Yongyu has not applied for a change of registration for a long time and did not assert her rights until the court took compulsory execution measures. The purpose was to help Lin Rongda evade execution. 4. Zhong Yongyu has separately sued Lin Rongda in another case to confirm the property right of the property in dispute. Concealing the fact that the property in dispute had been sealed up by the court according to law, she filed a separate confirmation of rights lawsuit, which does not comply with legal provisions. According to Article 26 of the "Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Reasonable Allocation and Scientific Operation of Execution Powers" (Fa Fa [2011] No. 15), the court receiving the case should not hear the confirmation of rights lawsuit between Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda. Any confirmation judgment or mediation document should also be revoked and cannot serve as the basis for determining this case. In summary, the real right of the property in dispute has not changed, and it still belongs to Lin Rongda. The execution court's execution measures against the property in dispute belonging to Lin Rongda are correct and lawful. The purpose of Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda filing this lawsuit is to evade execution. The court is requested to reject all of Zhong Yongyu's claims according to law to protect the lawful rights and interests of Wang Guang.

The court of first instance found through trial that Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda registered their marriage on June 28, 1972. On July 22, 1996, Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda signed a "Divorce Agreement", which stated: "Both parties now agree to go through the divorce procedures. The house built at No. 11 Xinlian Road, Jingmei Village, and the house with an area of 173 square meters on Heping Road, Chengguan, Shanghang County (house number not yet assigned) shall belong to the woman and her minor children. But they are only allowed to live in it and not to sell it."

On August 7, 1996, Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda went through the divorce procedures. The "Divorce Registration Application" and "Review and Handling Result" reflected that Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda were examined and approved for divorce by the marriage registration authority.

According to the "Shanghang County Private House Ownership Registration Application", the "House Ownership Certificate" (Hang Fang Quan Zi No. 06072), and the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" (Hang Guo Yong (1997) Zi No. 4468), the application stated that the property in dispute was newly built, with a land area of 172.8 square meters, and the year of completion was 1996. Meanwhile, the floor plans attached to both the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" and the "House Ownership Certificate" for the property in dispute were consistent with the floor plan attached to the "Shanghang County Private House Ownership Registration Application".

The four children of Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda, namely Lin Bisheng, Lin Xiaoyan, Lin Xiaojun, and Lin Lijuan, issued a "Statement", stating that they agreed that the property in dispute should belong to Zhong Yongyu, and that the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" and "House Ownership Certificate" should be directly changed to her name, and that any disputes or lawsuits arising therefrom should be fully handled by Zhong Yongyu.

The court of first instance also found that Lin Rongda stated in court hearings at Shanghang County People's Court on February 17, 2014 and March 24, 2014 that the land use right for the property in dispute was purchased from the Shanghang County Land and Resources Bureau in 1994, the building was completed and occupied in 1995, the application for the land use certificate was made to the land management department in 1996, and the land use certificate and house ownership certificate were not obtained until 1997. At the time of divorce, the two parties had agreed that the jointly owned property, i.e., the property in dispute, should belong to Zhong Yongyu and her minor children. Because the land was purchased in Lin Rongda's name, the issuing authority required it to be processed in his name. Originally, the house ownership could have been transferred to Zhong Yongyu's name, but this was never done. After the divorce, the property was occupied, used, and benefited from by Zhong Yongyu. The current house number of the property in dispute is No. 121 Heping Road, and at the time of divorce it was agreed to belong to Zhong Yongyu and her minor children.

The third party Li Jianhang stated that the ground floor shop of the property in dispute had been rented by him from Zhong Yongyu since February 2010, with a monthly rent of RMB 1,200, paid in cash every six months. According to evidence provided by Zhong Yongyu, such as the "Shanghang County Water Supply Company Water Sub-meter Card" and "Water Supply Company Water Account Card", the property in dispute under Lin Rongda's name was completed and occupied in February 1996.

The court of first instance held that Zhong Yongyu, filing a lawsuit for execution objection by a third party pursuant to Article 227 of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China", must provide evidence to prove that her substantive rights over the property in dispute are sufficient to obstruct the compulsory execution measures. The "Divorce Registration Application", "Divorce Agreement", and "Review and Handling Result" provided by Zhong Yongyu were all copied from the Shanghang County Archives, and their authenticity should be recognized. The content of these three documents reflects that Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda reached a divorce agreement through consultation and were approved by the administrative authority to go through the divorce registration. Although the "Marriage Registration Application" provided by Zhong Yongyu after the trial of first instance listed the applicant as "Zhong Yongyuegu", and she did not provide other evidence to prove that her former name was "Zhong Yongyuegu", whether a lawful marriage relationship existed between Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda is a matter that the administrative authority should have examined when handling their divorce registration. The administrative authority's review result of "meeting the conditions, granting (divorce registration)" should include the confirmation that a marriage relationship previously existed between them. Therefore, Wang Guang's arguments that the "Divorce Agreement" did not fill in the marriage certificate number and that Zhong Yongyu failed to provide evidence proving the existence of a lawful marriage relationship with Lin Rongda, and that the "Divorce Agreement" was therefore invalid, were unfounded and not supported by the court of first instance. The "Divorce Agreement" signed by Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda was voluntarily reached, its content did not violate any mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and the two parties had already dissolved their marriage relationship according to the agreement and with the approval of the administrative authority. Therefore, the divorce agreement should be recognized as legally valid.

Although the "Shanghang County Private House Ownership Registration Application" and the title certificates for the property in dispute provided by Zhong Yongyu showed that Lin Rongda applied for and obtained the title certificates for the property in dispute in 1997, the "Shanghang County Private House Ownership Registration Application" stated that the property was built in 1996. The water sub-meter card and water account card provided by Zhong Yongyu after the trial of first instance also showed that the property had water installation in February 1996 and had monthly water usage records. The above facts corroborated Lin Rongda's statements that the land for the property was purchased in 1994, the house was completed at the end of 1995, occupied in early 1996, and the land transfer procedures were completed and title certificates were obtained in 1997. This proves that the property in dispute was purchased and lawfully built during the marriage of Lin Rongda and Zhong Yongyu. According to Article 17 of the "Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China", it should be their jointly owned property.

In 1996, the two parties reached the "Divorce Agreement" through consultation, which stipulated that the property should belong to Zhong Yongyu and her children. This agreement was not only a division agreement for the jointly owned property but also, because it involved the dissolution of personal relationships, differed from a general agreement for the transfer of house ownership. Zhong Yongyu, as a co-owner of the property in dispute, enjoyed the real right over the property according to law. Her request to stop the compulsory execution measures against the property in dispute was supported by the court of first instance. According to the "Divorce Agreement" between Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda, the ownership of the property in dispute should be enjoyed by Zhong Yongyu and her four children. During the trial of first instance, although Zhong Yongyu provided the "Statements" of Lin Bisheng and four others, claiming that they were her legitimate children, since these four persons were not parties to this case, the "Statements" alone could not prove the identities of Lin Bisheng and others. Therefore, the "Statement" was insufficient to establish that the four children, including Lin Bisheng, mentioned in the "Divorce Agreement" had agreed to transfer the rights in the property in dispute to Zhong Yongyu. Under these circumstances, Zhong Yongyu's request in this case to adjudicate the property in dispute as belonging to her lacked sufficient basis and was not supported by the court of first instance.

In summary, pursuant to Article 17 and Article 39, paragraph 1 of the "Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China", Article 227 of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China", and Article 24 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Execution Procedure of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China", the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: 1. Execution of the property located at No. 121 Heping Road, Shanghang County, Fujian Province shall be stopped; 2. Zhong Yongyu's other claims are rejected. The case acceptance fee of RMB 100 shall be borne by Wang Guang.

Wang Guang, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, filed an appeal to this Court, requesting: 1. To set aside the first item of the civil judgment (2014) Min Min Chu Zi No. 7 of the Fujian High People's Court, and to change the judgment to reject all of Zhong Yongyu's claims; 2. The litigation costs of this case shall be borne by Zhong Yongyu. The main reasons are: 1. The real right of the property in dispute belongs to Lin Rongda. The court of first instance, instead of relying on the real estate title certificate, based its finding that Zhong Yongyu enjoyed the real right over the property and ordered the cessation of execution on the "Divorce Agreement" reached by the two parties in 1996 through consultation. This conclusion has no legal basis. 2. Even if, according to the view of the court of first instance, the ownership of the property in dispute is determined by the "Divorce Agreement", Zhong Yongyu's claims still cannot be sustained. (1) The area of the property in dispute referred to in the "Divorce Agreement" related to Zhong Yongyu and her children is only 173 square meters. However, according to the "House Ownership Certificate" for the property in dispute, the area of the property in dispute is 748.7 square meters. Zhong Yongyu only has a claim right to 173 square meters of the 748.7 square meters (173 square meters is approximately the area of one floor), not to the entire 748.7 square meters (and this right only refers to the right to use the 173 square meters). Therefore, execution of the property in dispute (especially the part beyond 173 square meters) cannot be stopped. (2) The content of the "Divorce Agreement" is "only allowed to live in, not to sell," meaning that Zhong Yongyu does not have the right to dispose of the property. Zhong Yongyu only has the right to live in and use the property, not ownership. Therefore, Zhong Yongyu actually has only the right to live in and use one-quarter of the property in dispute, which cannot prevent the auction and execution of the property in dispute. 3. Zhong Yongyu claimed that the "Divorce Agreement" was reached in 1996, but until the court sealed the property in dispute in 2011, a period of 15 years, Zhong Yongyu never applied for a change of registration. This fact proves that, according to the "Divorce Agreement", Zhong Yongyu did not obtain ownership of the property in dispute. The reason she raised an execution objection to the property in dispute 17 years later (Zhong Yongyu only raised the execution objection in 2013) is purely to assist Lin Rongda in evading execution.

Zhong Yongyu argued in her defense that her request for the court to suspend the enforcement measures against the disputed house was well-founded in law, and that the court of first instance had found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and the judgment should be upheld. First, the Divorce Agreement signed by Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda had a very clear allocation of ownership of the house, and after signing the Divorce Agreement, Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda also signed the Divorce Registration Application on August 7, 1996, which again specified that the "property disposal" method was "the house belongs to the wife." The Divorce Registration Application was a consensual act without malicious intent by both parties, a legal document filed with the administrative authority, which was lawful and valid, meaning that the entire house involved in the case belonged to the wife, and Zhong Yongyu was the owner (or at least a co-owner) of the disputed house. The provision in the Divorce Agreement that "only permitted to reside, not permitted to sell" was actually because Lin Rongda considered the possibility that after divorce he might remarry, and was worried that if the house were later sold, the basic livelihood of their four children would not be guaranteed. This provision was not a legal limitation on the real right of the house, but rather a "divorce condition" proposed by Lin Rongda from the perspective of protecting the children's interests. Even if one were to concede the point, the property division between Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda constituted a creditor-debtor relationship, which arose from the Divorce Agreement, and the subject matter of the debt was unique and definite — that is, the disputed house, falling under a specific debt. The debt dispute between Wang Guang and Lin Rongda arising from the equity transfer occurred 14 years after the divorce, falling under a generic debt, and it was formed later. Therefore, the specific debt takes precedence over the generic debt. Second, the "house located at Heping Road with an area of one hundred and seventy-three square meters (door number not yet assigned)" as recorded in the Divorce Agreement referred to the house at No. 121 Heping Road, and the area of one hundred and seventy-three square meters recorded in the Divorce Agreement was the land area of the house. 1. At the time of signing the Divorce Agreement, the disputed house had no door number, and the total gross floor area had not been actually measured; only the land area of the disputed house was known to be 172.8 square meters (rounded to 173 square meters). Therefore, the "one hundred and seventy-three square meters" in the agreement's phrase "the house located at Heping Road, Chengguan, Shanghang County, with an area of one hundred and seventy-three square meters" was merely an identifier in place of a door number. Moreover, the disputed house had four stories with a total gross floor area of 748.7 square meters, so the area per floor should also be 187.18 square meters, which was far from the 173 square meters recorded in the Divorce Agreement. If Lin Rongda and Zhong Yongyu had truly intended that one floor or 173 square meters of the disputed house belonged to the wife and her children, they should have clearly noted in the Divorce Registration Application which floor or what area belonged to the wife and her children. However, in reality, neither the Divorce Agreement nor the Divorce Registration Application contained such a note. Therefore, "one hundred and seventy-three square meters" referred to the land area of the house, not the area of one floor as claimed by Wang Guang. 2. Looking at the actual use of the disputed house, after her divorce from Lin Rongda, she single-handedly raised three children to adulthood in the disputed house, which had always been lived in and used by her and her children. Later, when it was leased out, it was Zhong Yongyu who collected the rent. After the divorce, Lin Rongda never lived in the disputed house. Moreover, according to common sense and Chinese rural customs, after a divorce, the man and woman would not continue to live in the same house, and it would be even less likely for one party to "lodge" in the other party's property. Third, the property certificate and land certificate for the disputed house in 1997 were issued in Lin Rongda's name because the relevant procedures for the land transfer had been handled with Lin Rongda as the registrant, so the title certificates were naturally issued in his name. Moreover, at that time, the Property Law had not yet been enacted or implemented, and ordinary people had little concept of the legal significance of registration of real property rights. A rural housewife with a low level of education would be even less likely to concern herself with how the property "two certificates" were handled. Zhong Yongyu was not at fault for the failure to complete the transfer of the house registration to her name to date.

Lin Rongda submitted his defense opinion, stating that he agreed with Zhong Yongyu's defense opinion.

The facts found by this court in the second instance are the same as those found by the court of first instance.

This court is of the opinion that this case is a lawsuit for execution objection filed by the person not involved in the case, Zhong Yongyu, in the enforcement of the effective judgment in the dispute over equity transfer between Wang Guang and Lin Rongda, against the subject matter of enforcement (the disputed house). The reason for seeking exclusion of enforcement is that before the equity transfer relationship arose, the disputed house had already been disposed of in the divorce agreement as jointly owned property between herself and Lin Rongda, to be owned by her and her four children. Therefore, whether Zhong Yongyu has a substantive right in the disputed house sufficient to prevent enforcement is the focus of the dispute in this case. This court is of the opinion that Zhong Yongyu has a right sufficient to preclude enforcement of the disputed house. The main reasons are as follows:

First, the existing evidence cannot prove that there was a malicious intent between Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda to collude in evading debts, and the intent of Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda in dissolving their marital relationship and in the relevant property agreements was genuine. According to the facts found in the original trial, the time of the equity transfer between Wang Guang and Lin Rongda was September 2009. The time when Wang Guang applied to the court of original trial for the sealing of the disputed house based on the effective judgment in that equity transfer dispute was June 2013, at which time the disputed house was registered in the personal name of the debtor, Lin Rongda. The three pieces of evidence provided by Zhong Yongdu in the first instance — photocopies of the Divorce Registration Application, the Divorce Agreement, and the Review and Processing Results from the Shanghang County Archives — can prove that the Divorce Agreement reached between Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda on July 22, 1996, had clearly assigned the disputed house, which was jointly owned property of the husband and wife, to Zhong Yongyu and her children. The aforementioned Divorce Agreement was voluntarily reached by both Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda, its content did not violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and the two had already dissolved their marital relationship in accordance with the agreement and with the approval of the administrative authority. Therefore, the court of first instance found the divorce agreement lawful and valid, which was not improper. Since the Divorce Agreement was signed first (July 1996), and the court's sealing of the disputed house for enforcement (June 2013) occurred later, with a gap of over ten years, Lin Rongda and Zhong Yongyu did not have the subjective malicious intent to evade debts by disposing of property through the divorce agreement. Accordingly, the act of Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda in disposing of their jointly owned property in the divorce agreement was also valid. Wang Guang's appeal argument that the divorce agreement between Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda constituted malicious evasion of debts cannot be established.

Second, concerning the content of Zhong Yongyu's claim right over the disputed house. According to evidence such as the Shanghang County Private House Ownership Registration Application, the House Ownership Certificate (Hang Fang Quan Zi No. 06072), and the State-owned Land Use Certificate (Hang Guo Yong (1997) Zi No. 4468), the land area of the disputed house is 172.8 square meters. Since at the time Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda signed the Divorce Agreement, the disputed house had not yet been assigned a door number nor its actual area measured, the provision in the Divorce Agreement that "...the house located at Heping Road, Chengguan, Shanghang County, with an area of one hundred and seventy-three square meters (door number not yet assigned) shall belong to the wife and her children" should be interpreted as meaning that the entire disputed house, not just 173 square meters thereof, should belong to Zhong Yongyu and her children. In particular, after the signing of the Divorce Agreement, Zhong Yongyu and her children have continuously actually possessed and used the disputed house. Therefore, Wang Guang's appeal argument that Zhong Yongyu only has a claim right over the 173 square meter portion of the disputed house and that the people's court should not stay enforcement of other parts of the house cannot be established.

Third, since there is no issue of malicious collusion to evade debts in the Divorce Agreement, and Zhong Yongdu has a claim right over the entire house involved in the case, the further question that needs to be discussed is whether the right of Zhong Yongyu over the disputed house based on the Divorce Agreement is sufficient to exclude enforcement.

In terms of the application of law, it should be noted that the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Execution Objections and Reconsideration Cases by the People's Courts is a regulation on how to handle cases when a party raises an execution objection during the execution procedure. Since the execution procedure needs to implement the enforceability of an effective judgment, a higher and more externalized standard of judgment should be adhered to when determining whether an execution objection is established. This standard of judgment is higher than the standard for determining whether a plaintiff can exclude enforcement in a lawsuit for execution objection.

Therefore, Articles 25 to 28 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Execution Objections and Reconsideration Cases by the People's Courts should be understood in the following sense: if the conditions listed in these provisions are met, the execution objection can be established; if the conditions are not met, the objection claimant's request in the lawsuit for execution objection may not necessarily fail either. Whether it is established should be determined by making a comprehensive comparison based on the specific circumstances of the case and the rights claimed by the objector, the effectiveness of the realization of the applying executor's claim, and the rights of the person subject to execution over the subject matter of enforcement, thereby determining whether the objector's right can exclude enforcement.

In this case, Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda signed the Divorce Agreement on July 22, 1996, stipulating that the disputed house should belong to Zhong Yongyu and her children. This provision was an agreement on property distribution upon the dissolution of the marriage relationship. Before the transfer of ownership of the disputed house was registered, Zhong Yongyu and her children enjoyed the right to request the registration of the change of ownership of the disputed house to their names. This right to request differs from Wang Guang's right to request in several respects, and therefore has the effect of excluding enforcement.

First, in terms of the time of establishment, this right to request arose much earlier than the monetary claim formed by Wang Guang due to the equity transfer dispute with Lin Rongda. Although the time of establishment of a claim does not affect the equality of claims, it does influence, in certain circumstances, whether the claim can continue to be performed and the order of such performance. For example, Article 10 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law for the Trial of Sales Contract Dispute Cases explicitly provides that, in the case of multiple sales contracts for special movable property entered into by the seller, where neither delivery has been taken nor ownership transfer registration has been completed, the continuing performance right of the buyer under the contract established earlier in law takes precedence over that of other buyers. By analogy, in the present case, it cannot at least be concluded that Wang Guang's claim, which arose later, has priority over Zhong Yongyu's claim, which arose earlier.

Second, in terms of content, Zhong Yongyu's right to request is directed at the specific disputed house, while Wang Guang's claim is a monetary claim not directed at any specific property. The disputed house merely served as Lin Rongda's liable property providing general security for Wang Guang's claim. Given that Zhong Yongyu is in possession of the disputed house, and with reference to the spirit of Article 10 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law for the Trial of Sales Contract Dispute Cases, her right to request the registration of the change of ownership of the disputed house to her name should also take precedence over Wang Guang's monetary claim.

Third, in terms of nature, the monetary claim between Wang Guang and Lin Rongda arose after the dissolution of the marital relationship between Lin Rongda and Zhong Yongyu, and is a personal debt of Lin Rongda. At the time this claim came into existence, the disputed house had effectively ceased to be part of Lin Rongda's liable property due to the agreement between Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda. Therefore, during the transaction between Wang Guang and Lin Rongda and throughout the process of forming the final monetary claim, the disputed house did not affect Lin Rongda's liable property. In this sense, even if Zhong Yongyu's right to request excludes enforcement of Wang Guang's claim, it does not adversely affect the realization of Wang Guang's claim.

Fourth, in terms of the root of origin, the disputed house was jointly owned property of Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda arising from lawful construction during the existence of their marital relationship. Upon the dissolution of the marital relationship between Zhong Yongyu and Lin Rongda, it was agreed that the disputed house should belong to Zhong Yongyu and her children. Functionally, this house has the function of providing living security for Zhong Yongyu and her children. Compared with Wang Guang's monetary claim, the right to request enjoyed by Zhong Yongyu and her children has a certain ethical priority.

In summary, this court is of the opinion that, based on the time, content, nature, and root of origin of the respective claims of Zhong Yongyu and Wang Guang, the right enjoyed by Zhong Yongyu over the disputed house should be sufficient to preclude enforcement of the disputed house in this case. The reasons for Zhong Yongyu's filing of the execution objection to preclude enforcement of the disputed house in this case are established. The judgment of the court of first instance to stay enforcement of the disputed house located at No. 121 Heping Road, Shanghang County, Fujian Province, was correct and should be upheld. The grounds for Wang Guang's appeal request to set aside that part of the judgment cannot be established, and this court does not support them.

In conclusion, the judgment of the first instance found the facts clearly and the result was correct. Pursuant to Paragraph 1, Item 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court hereby renders the following judgment:

Appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed.

The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 100 shall be borne by Wang Guang.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Yao Aihua

Trial Judge: Wang Yuying

Acting Trial Judge: Jiang Qiang

Date: January 10, 2016

Clerk: Wang Huixian
